differences.title: 1. INITIAL LOAD
differences.leftDesc: Server Components send only HTML, reducing initial load.
differences.rightDesc: Client Components ship JavaScript, increasing initial load.

differences.title: 2. INTERACTIVITY
differences.leftDesc: Server Components are static, less interactive by default.
differences.rightDesc: Client Components enable rich, dynamic user interfaces.

differences.title: 3. DATA FETCHING
differences.leftDesc: Fetch data directly on the server, securely.
differences.rightDesc: Fetch data in the browser, potentially less secure.

differences.title: 4. ROUTING
differences.leftDesc: Navigation happens on the server, faster initial page loads.
differences.rightDesc: Client-side routing for seamless transitions after initial load.

differences.title: 5. RENDERING
differences.leftDesc: Rendered on the server before sending to the client.
differences.rightDesc: Rendered directly in the user's browser.

differences.title: 6. STATE MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: State management is primarily server-driven or passed as props.
differences.rightDesc: Offers robust client-side state management solutions.

differences.title: 7. COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Leads to smaller client bundles and easier deployment.
differences.rightDesc: Requires managing hydration and client-side logic.
